                    ### Question
                    A 10-year-old boy comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He was diagnosed with asthma one year ago and uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. His mother reports that he has had shortness of breath on exertion and a dry cough 3–4 times per week over the past month. Pulmonary examination shows expiratory wheezing in all lung fields. Treatment with low-dose inhaled mometasone is initiated. Which of the following recommendations is most appropriate to prevent complications from this treatment?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole use three times weekly
opb. Pantoprazole use prior to meals
opc. Minimizing use of a spacer
opd. Oral rinsing after medication administration
ope. Weight-bearing exercise three times weekly

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
To prevent complications from low-dose inhaled mometasone treatment for asthma, the most appropriate recommendation is oral rinsing after medication administration. This is crucial to reduce the risk of oral thrush associated with inhaled corticosteroid use, as supported by standard medical practice.
